**<mark>ICSG PRESS RELEASE                                    Date Issued: 3</mark>**<sup>**rd**</sup> **<mark>August 2010</mark>** 



# **Release of ICSG 2010 Statistical Yearbook** 

The International Copper Study Group released its 2010 Statistical Yearbook covering world copper supply and demand data for the 10-year period 2000- 2009. 

According to ICSG data, world copper mine production rose by 19% during the 10-year period from 13.2 million metric tonnes (Mt) in 2000 to 15.8 Mt in 2009: copper in concentrates rose by 15% while solvent extraction-electrowinning (SX-EW) production rose by 41%. The SX-EW share of total mine production increased from 18% in 2000 to 21% in 2009. While the mine capacity utilization rate averaged around 88% over the period, the rate fell sharply during latter years. Over the 2008-2009 period, as a result of numerous factors including lower head grades, labour unrest, technical problems, and temporary shutdowns or production cuts, capacity utilization averaged only 82% and mine production grew by an average of only 0.9% per year (%/yr): Mine production grew 2.3%/yr during the preceding 8 years and averaged 2% over the 10-year period. Notable changes in annual mine production over 2000-2010 included an almost 800,000 t increase in Chilean production, a combined 1.8 MT increase due to the revival of the African copper belt and expansions/new projects in Peru and China, and a combined decline of about 400,000 t (21%) in Mexican and U.S. production. On a regional basis, production increased by 125% in Africa (600,000 t), 32% in Latin America (1.7 Mt), 28% in Asia (700,000 t) and 6% in Europe (90,000 t), declined by 22% in North America (530,000 t) and remained practically unchanged in Oceania (-1%), 

Over the 10-year period, annual world refined production rose by 24% from 14.8 Mt in 2000 to 18.4 Mt in 2009, with an annual average growth rate of 2.5%. Primary and secondary refined production increased by 22% and 39%, respectively. The share of secondary production in total refined production averaged 13.8% over the period and, owing to the combined effects of concentrate shortages and higher refined prices, averaged 15.4% in recent years. Over the full 10-year period, China and India’s annual refined production together more than tripled, increasing by 2.8 Mt to 4.1 Mt and by 455,000 t to 715,000 t, respectively. Chilean production increased by 600,000 t to 3.3 Mt and significant increases in Bulgaria, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Zambia together added around half a million tons of annual world refined production. In North America, production fell in the United States and Canada by 35% (630,000 t) and by 40% (215,000 t) respectively. Refined production in the EU rose by 7% to 2.5 Mt. 

World annual refined copper usage increased by 20% over the 10-year period from 15.2 Mt to 18.2 Mt (annual growth rate of 2.1%). Growth was driven by China<sup>1</sup> where apparent usage over the 10-year period increased

by around 5.3 Mt (+280%). World usage excluding China in fact decreased by 17% (3.3 Mt) during the period, with particularly weak usage in 2008 and 2009 due to the world economic recession. On a regional basis, usage grew in Africa by 200% (200,000 t), in Asia ex-China by 7% (260,000 t), and in Europe ex-EU by 55% (270,000 t). Usage decreased in the Americas by 40% (1.8 Mt), in the EU by 30% (1.2 Mt) and in Oceania by 25% (45,000 t). The ICSG 2010 Statistical Yearbook is included as part of the ICSG Monthly Bulletin annual subscription and is also available for sale as a separate issue (€200 for orders originating from ICSG member countries and €300 for other orders). 1 China’s apparent copper usage is based only on reported data (production + net trade +/- SHFE stock changes+/-industry stock changes, if reported) and does not take into account changes in unreported stocks [State Reserve Bureau (SRB), producer, consumer and merchant/trader], which may be significant during periods of stocking or de-stocking. ## **World Refined Copper Usage and Supply Trends, 2000-2009** Thousand metric tonnes, copper ||**2000**|**2001**|**2002**|**2003**|**2004**|**2005**|**2006**|**2007**|**2008**|**2009**
